title: Meta Enables US Users to Video Chat with Their Muse AI Avatar, Says TechCrunch
body:
Meta has rolled out a new feature that lets anyone in the United States video‑chat with its AI companion, Muse, using a customizable animated avatar. Dubbed “Muse Voice,” the service transforms the text‑based chatbot into a visual presence that can appear on a phone screen, a laptop webcam, or a future wearable device that Meta describes as a “digital Tamagotchi.” The move marks the latest step in the company’s push to embed generative AI into everyday social interactions, and it signals a broader strategy to monetize AI assistants beyond the traditional text‑only format.

The Muse avatar is built on Meta’s family of large language models, which have been refined over the past two years to handle conversational nuances, factual grounding, and multimodal inputs such as images and voice. Users can choose from a library of cartoon‑style characters, adjust facial expressions, and even modify the avatar’s clothing, creating a personalized “digital twin” that responds in real time to spoken queries. The feature is currently available through the Meta app on iOS and Android, and it integrates with the company’s existing messaging and video platforms, allowing seamless handoffs between text chat, voice calls, and now live video calls with the AI.

Industry analysts see the launch as a testbed for a more ambitious vision: a wearable that projects the Muse avatar onto a user’s wrist or chest, turning the AI into a constant companion. The prototype, unveiled in a recent developer preview, resembles a small, animated figurine that can be attached to clothing or a smartwatch band. Meta hopes the device will appeal to younger users who are already accustomed to avatar‑centric experiences in gaming and social media. By making the avatar both interactive and portable, the company aims to create a new revenue stream through hardware sales, subscription tiers for premium avatar skins, and potential advertising partnerships embedded within the AI’s dialogue.

Critics, however, warn that turning a conversational AI into a visual character could blur the line between human and machine interaction, raising concerns about privacy, data collection, and the psychological impact of anthropomorphized bots. Meta has pledged that all voice and video data will be processed on its servers with end‑to‑end encryption, but the company’s track record on data handling continues to attract scrutiny from regulators. Consumer‑rights groups have called for clearer disclosures about how Muse’s responses are generated and whether the avatar can be used to influence user behavior, especially in the context of targeted advertising.

From a competitive standpoint, Meta’s move puts it in direct contention with other tech giants that are experimenting with AI‑driven avatars. Google’s Gemini and Apple’s Siri are both exploring visual representations, while startups such as Soul Machines and Replika have already offered lifelike digital companions. Meta’s advantage lies in its massive social graph and the integration of Muse across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, giving the avatar a built‑in audience that few rivals can match. The company’s aggressive rollout—making the feature free for all U.S. users—suggests it is betting on network effects to accelerate adoption and gather the usage data needed to refine the models.

Looking ahead, the success of Muse Voice will likely hinge on how well Meta can balance novelty with utility. If users find the avatar helpful for tasks like scheduling, language tutoring, or mental‑wellness check‑ins, the feature could evolve from a gimmick into a staple of digital life. Conversely, if the experience feels superficial or raises too many privacy red flags, adoption may stall. As the AI avatar market matures, Meta’s strategy of pairing software with a dedicated wearable could set a precedent for a new class of personal AI devices, reshaping how people interact with machines in both private and public spaces. The coming months will reveal whether Muse’s animated presence will become a ubiquitous companion or remain a niche experiment in the ever‑expanding AI landscape.
